text:
- chief complaint: right foot pain after a tennis fall, with the patient unable to bear weight.
- history of present illness: the patient fell onto the right foot while volleying in doubles tennis and twisted it. Pain began immediately and the patient was helped off the field. The injury occurred about two days ago. Self-care has included compression wrap, ice, elevation, and ibuprofen, which helps only partially. No numbness or loss of sensation. Prior injury was to the left foot.
- physical examination: vitals normal (BP 125/70, RR 18, T 97.1°F, SpO2 100%, HR ~60). Heart and abdomen normal. Mild stridor noted on lung exam, with no wheezes or rales. Right foot shows bruising on plantar and dorsal surfaces, swelling, midfoot tenderness, warmth, and positive piano key test at the first and second metatarsals. Neurovascular status intact. X-ray shows subtle dorsal displacement at the second metatarsal base, 3 mm first-second metatarsal separation, and a bony fragment in the Lisfranc joint.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: right foot pain, inability to bear weight, bruising, swelling, warmth. No numbness, tingling, or sensory loss.
- new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: N/A.
- follow-up instructions: MRI ordered to assess the fracture and ligament injury. Surgery (plates and screws) recommended as day surgery; the patient must have a driver. Follow-up in clinic in about one week. Cast and crutches for 6–8 weeks, non-weight-bearing, then gradual weight-bearing. Physical therapy after surgery. Surgical consent paperwork and risk discussion to follow. Out for the rest of the season.
